_doc: Revert-verify mutants for issue #4551 / req 60ed88e7 (vault-exodev task c223e6ef, RFC 14217015 P1.5): a SPARQL BIND extends the group prefix at its position. Each mutant removes one guarantee and must redden exactly the axes in `expect` (pairwise distinct within the spec). `red_re` anchors on the jest failure header `● <suite> › Bn @req` (ITRV §A44/§A104). `tree`/`subject` are placeholders — run the matrix on a copy with the paths substituted (§A145). Subject: QueryExecutor — bind-join predicate substitution and the IRI value of BIND(<iri>).
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/infrastructure/sparql/executors/QueryExecutor.ts

QE1_no_predicate_substitution._note: The join no longer substitutes a bound PREDICATE: same rows, but every left solution scans every triple. Type-preserving: an impossible type tag.

QE2_no_fromBinding_mark._note: The substituted predicate is not marked fromBinding — it is widened like a constant.

QE3_bind_iri_as_string._note: The marked BIND(<iri>) still binds the string (the consumer half of PT4).

QE4_subquery_scope_ignored._note: A subquery's unprojected variables are substituted again (the pre-review behaviour): a leading BIND captures a variable the subquery does not project. Type-preserving (`length < 0`, never true).
QE4_subquery_scope_ignored.from: if (node.type === 'project') return sliced ? new Set() : new Set(node.variables);
QE4_subquery_scope_ignored.to: if (node.type === 'project' && node.variables.length < 0) return sliced ? new Set() : new Set(node.variables);

QE5_slice_substituted._note: A LIMIT/OFFSET subquery is substituted into again by the bind join: a bound outer value restricts the subquery before its slice, changing which rows the slice keeps (review round 2, MEDIUM). B27: the shared variable is visible again, so the join binds per left row instead of running the subquery once.

QE6_slice_rule_everywhere._note: The slice rule applies to every substitution, not only the join (the round-2 code): EXISTS / NOT EXISTS / IF(EXISTS) and LATERAL over a LIMIT subquery stop being correlated (review round 3, H1). Shares QE5's anchor (§A94) — the difference is in `to`. Round 4: the correlated scope never withholds from a slice under this mutation, so the EXISTS inside a join operand (B38) and the LIMIT subquery joined inside an EXISTS pattern (B42) lose their correlation too.

QE7_exists_join_scope._note: EXISTS substitutes with the join scope — the slice withholds the outer solution (H1, the EXISTS half). Round 4: B42 is a top-level EXISTS too — its pattern joins a LIMIT subquery, which the join scope withholds from.

QE8_lateral_join_scope._note: LATERAL substitutes with the join scope — a nested LIMIT subquery stops being top-N per outer row (H1, the LATERAL half).

QE9_hidden_shared_counted._note: The join counts a variable hidden inside a sliced subquery as shared: same rows, but the subquery is re-run unchanged once per left row (review round 3, M1: 1.1 s → 6.6 s).

QE10_nested_exists_join_scope._note: An EXISTS inside a join operand inherits the join scope (the pre-round-4 behaviour): its LIMIT subquery takes no outer value, the bind join already replaced the shared variable in the operand's own patterns, so the EXISTS loses its correlation — every row kept / none (review round 4, HIGH-2; reviewer's XQE1).
QE10_nested_exists_join_scope.to: expr.pattern = this.substituteInOperation(expr.pattern as AlgebraOperation, bindings, scope);

QE11_right_recursion_join_scope._note: The scope is not carried into the RIGHT child of a nested operation: a LIMIT subquery joined inside an EXISTS pattern is treated with the join scope and loses the outer value (review round 4, MEDIUM-1; reviewer's XQE3).
QE11_right_recursion_join_scope.from: opRecord.right = this.substituteInOperation(opRecord.right as AlgebraOperation, bindings, scope);
